cards.noteEnglish: English 'the fruit' and Spanish la fruta are mass nouns. French normally uses the plural les fruits for fruit in general; un fruit is one piece. The Reader's des fruits frais uses the same plural.
As Spanish té (tea) differs from te (you), French thé (tea) differs from the pronoun te (you): thé has an h and an accent.

cards.english: Do you have fresh orange juice?
cards.french: Vous avez du jus d'orange pressé ?
cards.noteEnglish: Pressé renders the source's natural: freshly squeezed, not from a carton. Vous covers the source's tienen (ustedes: you all / the café) as well as polite singular you. Avoir expresses possession here, as tener does in Spanish.

cards.french: Il y a du pain grillé ?
cards.noteEnglish: Il y a stays the same for singular and plural (there is / there are), like Spanish hay.

cards.french: J'ai besoin d'une serviette, s'il vous plaît.
cards.noteEnglish: Avoir besoin de + noun does the work of Spanish necesitar. De becomes d' before a vowel: d'une.

cards.english: I'd like a tea without sugar.
cards.french: Je voudrais un thé sans sucre.
cards.noteEnglish: Je voudrais translates the English face 'I'd like'. It is not the form-for-form match of the Spanish line: quiero is literally je veux (I want). Je voudrais corresponds to quisiera, which the source note gives as the softer, more polite alternative. Je veux sounds blunt to a server in French, so je voudrais is the usual way to order.

cards.english: Do you have to pay at the register?
cards.french: Il faut payer à la caisse ?
cards.noteEnglish: Il faut + infinitive is impersonal (one must / you have to), like Spanish hay que + infinitive.
French says avoir faim, as Spanish says tener hambre ('I have hunger'). Très goes before faim.

reader.english: In a café in Oaxaca, Emma tells the server Luis: I'm very hungry.
reader.french: Dans un café à Oaxaca, Emma dit au serveur Luis : J'ai très faim.
reader.spanishSource: En un café de Oaxaca, Emma le dice al mesero Luis: Tengo mucha hambre.

reader.english: Emma: Do you have fresh orange juice?
reader.french: Emma : Vous avez du jus d'orange pressé ?

reader.english: Luis: Yes, and there is also fresh fruit with breakfast.
reader.french: Luis : Oui, et il y a aussi des fruits frais avec le petit-déjeuner.
reader.spanishSource: Luis: Sí, y también hay fruta fresca con el desayuno.

reader.french: Emma : Il y a du pain grillé ?

reader.english: Luis: Yes, the toast comes with butter and jam.
reader.french: Luis : Oui, le pain grillé est servi avec du beurre et de la confiture.
reader.spanishSource: Luis: Sí, el pan tostado viene con mantequilla y mermelada.

reader.english: Emma: I'd like a tea without sugar and a spoon, please.
reader.french: Emma : Je voudrais un thé sans sucre et une cuillère, s'il vous plaît.
reader.spanishSource: Emma: Quiero un té sin azúcar y una cuchara, por favor.

reader.english: Emma: I also need a fork and a napkin, please.
reader.french: Emma : J'ai aussi besoin d'une fourchette et d'une serviette, s'il vous plaît.
reader.spanishSource: Emma: También necesito un tenedor y una servilleta, por favor.

reader.english: Luis: Sure, and you have to pay at the register at the end.
reader.french: Luis : Bien sûr, et il faut payer à la caisse à la fin.
reader.spanishSource: Luis: Claro, y hay que pagar en la caja al final.

sourceNotes: Setting and title follow the source: Desayuno en Oaxaca, with Emma and the server Luis. Draft French title: Petit-déjeuner à Oaxaca, held in readerTitle.
All 15 English card faces and kinds are copied from SOURCE.words in source order (9 terms, then 6 phrases). Each card carries its Spanish face and source index.
All 8 Reader English lines are copied from READER.native. Each line carries its Spanish target line and index.
Card and Reader indices are 0-based. Mode, form and speaking answers are held as refs or hidden metadata, never in prompt text.
Focus mapping: tener (possession and tener hambre) to avoir; hay to il y a; necesitar to avoir besoin de; hay que + infinitive to il faut + infinitive.

Querer contrast: the Spanish source uses quiero on card 12 and Reader line 5, while the English faces say 'I'd like'. The French follows the English with je voudrais. Quiero is literally je veux. Je voudrais corresponds to quisiera, which the source note names as the softer form. The English faces are unchanged.
Source 'natural' (freshly squeezed, not from a carton) is rendered pressé on card 9 and Reader line 1.
Source la fruta / 'the fruit' (mass) is rendered les fruits on card 4, consistent with des fruits frais in Reader line 2.

Reader line 2 uses avec le petit-déjeuner for source con el desayuno / 'with breakfast'. Reader line 4 uses est servi avec for source viene con / 'comes with'; this is a wording shift for idiom, not a literal match.

Notes marked noteBasis 'source-note' adapt a note in SOURCE.words. 'source-focus' notes explain the lesson focus. 'adjudication' notes are added by this pass. Cards with note null have no source note.

This adjudication is an AI pass made without tools or repository access. Parity was checked only against the SOURCE and READER text pasted into the request. It is not a qualified review.
qualifiedReviewResiduals: Every French string is an unreviewed AI draft. No native or qualified French reviewer has checked any of it, and this adjudication is not a qualified review. All top-level and per-item gates stay false.
No tools or repository files were used. Parity was checked only against the pasted SOURCE and READER, so a human diff against the repository source is still needed.
Pressé for 'natural' / 'fresh' needs confirmation. Alternatives a reviewer may prefer are du jus d'orange frais or une orange pressée.
Card 4 les fruits pairs a French plural with the English face 'the fruit'. A reviewer or the owner should confirm this over le fruit.
Spelling of petit-déjeuner: the hyphenated noun is accepted by some references, while others prefer petit déjeuner. This affects readerTitle and Reader line 2.
Reader line 4 est servi avec is not a literal match for viene con / 'comes with'. A reviewer should confirm it over vient avec.
Reader line 0 uses à Oaxaca for de Oaxaca / 'in Oaxaca', and a colon with direct speech and no guillemets. A reviewer should confirm the style.
Questions use rising intonation (Vous avez … ?, Il y a … ?, Il faut … ?). A reviewer should confirm this register over Est-ce que forms.
La serviette also means towel, and no disambiguating note is kept. Mexican Spanish mesero is rendered by the general French serveur.
The spaces before ? and : are ordinary spaces. A typographic no-break space policy is undecided.
